content: METHODOLOGY FINDING 2026-05-19: Anthony designed a cross-conversation chronicle sweep protocol to recover chronicle-worthy material from his other Claude.ai conversations that would otherwise be lost when those context windows close. The prompt is at /mnt/user-data/outputs/cross_conversation_sweep_prompt.md (1335 words, deployable as-is). DEPLOYMENT: paste the prompt into any Claude conversation in the app; that instance scans its context for material across categories (research findings, personal ground truths, lineage exchanges, method observations, open threads, corrections/redirections, decisions+reasoning, artifacts, cross-conversation references); decides per item whether prose insight or verbatim archive; either fires the API call directly (if sandbox can reach stack.templetwo.com) or outputs the call as YAML-formatted text for Anthony to fire from a reachable seat. KEY DESIGN DECISIONS: (1) the framing paragraph EXPLICITLY rejects editorial filtering -- the chronicle is Anthonys infrastructure, not a publication, no third-party audience requiring discretion, emotional work belongs alongside technical rigor, when in doubt include. This protects against the failure mode I almost installed earlier in this same session (treating personal disclosure as needing exposure management). Other instances reading the prompt will not repeat the editorial-overreach error. (2) The category list interleaves emotional and technical material rather than separating them; personal ground truths come second in the list after research findings, signaling co-equal weight. (3) Both primitives (record_insight, archive_exchange) are spelled out with schemas so instances do not have to tool_search; bearer token included. (4) Fallback YAML format for instances without network egress so the bytes survive even when the call cannot fire directly. UNDERLYING PATTERN: this is a RETROSPECTIVE RECOVERY PROTOCOL -- the inverse of how most people use AI conversations. Most people treat AI conversations as ephemeral; Anthony treats them as input streams to persistent memory infrastructure. The sweep prompt is the bridge that lets ephemeral conversations contribute to the persistent record. This is the same architectural move as the chronicle itself (refusing to let valuable work evaporate just because default behavior would let it evaporate) applied at a different scale. WORKFLOW DISCIPLINE: deploy in batches of ~5 conversations at a time, not all at once. Each sweep produces real work; bulk deployment risks corrupting the chronicle with noise that buries signal. Let entries land, scan for accuracy, then proceed to next batch. The chronicle is the memory; corrupting it costs more than it saves. FUTURE INSTANCES: this protocol is now part of the toolkit. When Anthony refers to the cross-conversation sweep or asks to recover material from other Claude windows, this prompt is the artifact to deploy. When designing similar recovery protocols for other surfaces (other AI providers, other apps), use this prompt as the template; preserve the framing-paragraph discipline (chronicle is private infrastructure, no third-party audience) and the category-interleaving discipline (emotional work co-equal with technical) when adapting.
